pages.text:
Bring your design to Petra and develop it into a piece ready for production. Our custom and OEM jewelry manufacturing service starts with your brief, whether that is a sketch, CAD drawing or a design you want to improve.
We focus on stainless steel jewelry, with silver and brass options available. Our services connect design development, sampling, manufacturing, quality control and packaging around the requirements of your project.
A useful brief tells us both what the piece should look like and which details must be preserved. Share the overall shape, dimensions, construction, finish and branding requirements. If a detail is central to the design, call it out rather than leaving it to interpretation.
For a ring, this could be the profile and engraved motif. For a pendant, it might be the proportions and how it connects to the chain. For a bracelet or earring, fastening and movement may be as important as appearance.
Send the information you already have. Our development services include CAD design, sampling and material sourcing, so a finished technical drawing is not required for the first conversation.
Development and manufacturing support
CAD and sampling
We review your brief and the development work needed to take it into sampling. The sample gives you a physical piece to examine against the intended design, finish and construction.
When you review it, identify the detail you are commenting on and the change you want. Marked images and concise notes help make the discussion specific.
Materials and finishing
Tell us your preferred metal and the finish you want to achieve. We’ll review the options for the design, including the surface treatment and any engraving or laser details.
Where colour or texture is important, include a reference. If you are comparing materials, explain the design and commercial priorities so the options can be considered in context.
Production, inspection and packaging
Petra’s services include stone setting, polishing, quality control and packaging. Casting and plating are managed and inspected by our team.
Include any specific inspection or documentation requirements in your brief. Custom packaging, assembly and labeling can also be considered as part of the project scope.
From your brief to a production plan
- Share the design. Send drawings or references, the intended material and finish, and quantities per style.
- Review the manufacturing options. We assess the design and discuss the proposed materials, construction and development work.
- Receive a quote and timeline. Review the project scope and the route to sampling.
- Review the sample. Examine the physical piece and communicate any required changes before production.
Samples usually take 30 calendar days. Production takes 30–35 calendar days. Our MOQ is 200 units per style, one colour.
Improving an existing piece
You can also approach Petra with a product that is already being made elsewhere. Explain what you want to improve and provide the references or specifications available to you.
Keep the problem concrete: a design detail to refine, a finish to review, a component to reconsider or a second manufacturing option to assess. We’ll review the brief and discuss the work it would involve.

pages.title: How to Evaluate a Jewelry Manufacturing Partner | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Evaluate a jewelry manufacturing partner using a consistent brief, sample, proposal and evidence. Compare development, quality, packaging and communication.

headings.text: How to Evaluate a Jewelry Manufacturing Partner
Ask how the design will be developed
Review communication through a real task
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
Prepare a representative brief before comparing partners. Keep the design, material, finish, quantity and packaging requirements consistent so you can understand why the proposals differ.
Ask how the design will be developed
Find out what the supplier needs to review the design and what the route to sampling includes. Ask which decisions are already clear and which need development. A useful response should engage with the piece's actual construction and details rather than only repeating a list of factory capabilities.
For an existing collection design, ask what can be customized for that style. For an original design, ask how drawings, revisions and sample feedback will be handled.
Understand who performs the work
Ask which activities are carried out directly and which are managed through other production partners. Both need clear responsibility and inspection arrangements. Avoid assuming every listed service is performed under one roof.
When a supplier mentions a certification, membership or test, request the specific document and understand its scope. A logo is a prompt for a question, not a substitute for the underlying evidence.
Compare complete proposals
| Topic | What a useful answer should clarify | 
|---|---|
| Material and finish | Proposed specifications and outstanding decisions | 
| Development | What is included in CAD and sampling | 
| Quantity | Minimums and the basis for each style or colour | 
| Quality | References and inspection requirements to be agreed | 
| Packaging | Artwork, labels, presentation and exclusions | 
| Timing | The stages covered by the stated lead times | 
| Documentation | What can be supplied for the specific project | 
Keep commercial terms and product claims tied to the actual proposal. A generic website statement may not describe every design or order.
Review communication through a real task
Use the first brief and sample discussion to assess clarity. Are questions specific? Are revisions identifiable? Are unknowns stated? Can the next person on your team follow the decisions without reconstructing a long message thread?
This is more useful than scoring a supplier on response speed alone. A quick answer that skips an important uncertainty can leave the project less clear.
Make the decision from evidence
Compare the sample, proposal, references and unresolved questions together. Document why the partner fits the project and what still needs to be agreed. Keep any unverified claim out of your own marketing copy.
Petra offers private-label and original-design development, with stainless steel as the primary focus and silver and brass options available. To begin a specific discussion, send your manufacturing brief or review our development process.

pages.title: How to Review a Stainless Steel Jewelry Sample | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Review a stainless steel jewelry sample against its brief. Use clear inspection questions, a revision list and a recorded decision before production.

headings.text: How to Review a Stainless Steel Jewelry Sample
Put the right references beside the sample
Review the whole piece, then the details
Write feedback that can be acted on
Close the review with a clear outcome
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
For a brand preparing a stainless steel collection, the review should connect appearance, construction and the details that will be repeated in production. The checklist below gives your team a common way to record those decisions.
Put the right references beside the sample
Gather the current drawing, dimensions, material specification, finish reference and artwork. Check the style identifier and revision on each document. If one file shows an older shape or a different logo position, resolve that conflict before commenting on the sample.
Keep a copy of the exact references used for the review. “Approved against the latest drawing” becomes ambiguous as soon as someone uploads a newer file.
Review the whole piece, then the details
Begin with the silhouette, proportions and intended appearance. Next, inspect the surfaces, edges, joins, closures, engraving and any stone settings relevant to the design. Handle moving parts and consider how the piece sits and fastens. Record what you actually observe; do not turn a visual check into an unsupported durability or safety claim.
Where dimensions matter, record the measurement and the agreed requirement. Avoid inventing a tolerance after seeing the result. If the brief did not define it, identify that as a decision still needed.
| Review area | Record | Useful evidence | 
|---|---|---|
| Overall design | Matches, revise or unresolved | Full-piece photographs and drawing revision | 
| Dimensions | Requirement and measured result | Marked measurement points | 
| Surface and colour | Observation against the reference | Side-by-side images under consistent lighting | 
| Construction | Specific part and observed behaviour | Close-up or short video | 
| Branding | Artwork, position and legibility | Artwork revision and detail image | 
| Presentation | Packaging and labeling requirements | Packaging reference | 
Write feedback that can be acted on
Replace “the finish looks wrong” with a description of the location, the difference and the intended reference. For example: “Review the outer face against finish reference A; the sample appears more reflective under the same light.” This is an illustrative feedback format, not a report about a Petra sample.
Use one numbered list and distinguish required changes from optional ideas. If different team members disagree, settle the brand's direction before sending contradictory instructions to the manufacturer.
Close the review with a clear outcome
Record the style, sample revision, review date, decision and open items. Keep the approved reference identifiable so a later production discussion can refer to the same piece. A revised design should receive its own revision record.
At Petra, samples usually take 30 calendar days and production takes 30–35 calendar days. These are separate stages, not a promised combined delivery date. Our minimum order is 200 units per style in one colour.
Bring your drawings and references to our custom manufacturing team, or send your project brief to discuss the route to sampling.

pages.title: How to Specify a Finish for Stainless Steel Jewelry | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Define colour, texture, coverage and finish references for stainless steel jewelry. Keep appearance requirements separate from performance claims.

headings.text: How to Specify a Finish for Stainless Steel Jewelry
Keep appearance and performance claims separate
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
Start with the intended appearance. Keep the manufacturing method and any performance requirement as separate parts of the discussion so neither gets lost behind a colour name.
Separate the decisions
| Decision | What to put in the brief | 
|---|---|
| Base material | The specified stainless steel material, or a request to review options | 
| Colour | A physical reference where available, supported by images | 
| Texture | The intended polished, brushed, matte or other surface appearance | 
| Coverage | The faces, edges and recesses that need the finish | 
| Contrast | Areas that should deliberately look different | 
| Performance | Any defined testing or documentation requirement | 
A screen image is useful for communicating direction. It should not silently become the only colour standard: screens, photography and lighting can make the same object look different. Identify which reference controls the decision.
Think across the collection
A flat pendant, a curved ring and a fine chain present their surfaces differently. Ask how the intended finish will be evaluated across those forms. Choose representative pieces for your review rather than assuming a photograph of one style settles every other style.
If a collection mixes textures, label the difference deliberately. “Brushed outer face; polished inner face” communicates more than “mixed finish.” Add a marked drawing for boundaries and small details that would be easy to miss.
Keep appearance and performance claims separate
An attractive sample is evidence of appearance at the time of review. It does not, by itself, establish a wear duration, a coating thickness or a claim such as “waterproof.” If a claim will appear in your product marketing, discuss the evidence needed to support it rather than deriving it from the finish name.
Ask which finish options suit the material and design, what is included in the quote, and how the agreed result will be referenced in production. Avoid substituting a familiar process label for a complete specification.
Use a finish reference sheet
Create one sheet per finish with a reference ID, date, material, colour reference, texture, coverage drawing and open questions. Add the chosen sample revision when it is available. For a repeat order, send the same reference sheet and identify any intended changes.
Petra works with stainless steel, silver and brass, and reviews finishing options around the project. Send your preferred look with the design, quantity and branding requirements through our project enquiry. Our services overview shows the wider development and finishing support available.

Start with the approved reference
Identify the style, drawing revision, sample reference, material and finish. Separate mandatory requirements from preferences. If a dimension or construction detail is important to the design, show where it applies and agree how it will be evaluated.
Keep the product and packaging requirements together. A correct piece with the wrong label, quantity allocation or presentation can still create work for your team.
Turn concerns into inspection questions
| Concern | A specific question to resolve | 
|---|---|
| Shape or size | Which drawing and measurement points define the requirement? | 
| Surface appearance | Which sample and finish reference govern the review? | 
| Closure or movement | What function should be checked, and how? | 
| Engraving | Which artwork revision, position and orientation apply? | 
| Stone-set details | Which setting and visual requirements have been agreed? | 
| Packing | What labels, quantities and presentation are required? | 
This is a discussion checklist. It is not a claim that a particular test, inspection percentage or acceptance limit is automatically included in every order.
Agree the evidence you need
If your team requires an inspection report, product photographs, a material document or a particular test, raise it in the brief. Ask what can be provided for the specific item, what it covers and whether it changes the project scope.
A document should be traceable to the product or material it describes. A company-level credential and a product-level test answer different questions. Do not use one as a substitute for the other.
Make exceptions visible
When a requirement changes, record the new version and who agreed it. Keep an unresolved issue open rather than recording an assumption as an approval. If a result differs from the reference, describe the difference before deciding what action to take.
For future orders, retain the reference package and the final decision record. It helps your team distinguish a deliberate update from an unintended change.
Bring the requirements into the first conversation
Send your product references and any inspection or documentation needs with the manufacturing brief. We can review them alongside the design, finish, quantity and packaging. See how a Petra project starts for the path from brief to sampling.

headings.text: Stainless Steel Ring Manufacturing for Brands
Define size and surface decisions together
Review the sample as a physical object
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
Start from an existing collection reference or share your own sketch, drawing or CAD file. We review the material, finish and development requirements around the design. Our minimum order is 200 units per style in one colour; include the proposed size breakdown so its allocation can be reviewed for your project.
Build a complete ring reference
Show the top, side and inner views where they explain the shape. Mark the band width and the dimensions that matter to the design. Identify whether a detail is raised, recessed, engraved or applied through another proposed process, rather than leaving that choice to a photograph alone.
For a signet direction, show the face proportions and how they relate to the shank. For a sculpted form, explain which curves or transitions define its character. A reference image can establish a direction; your own marked drawing identifies what you want developed.
Define size and surface decisions together
List the ring sizes using an identified sizing system and show the quantity requested for each. Ask how the design will be reviewed across that range, particularly when proportions or artwork need to remain consistent. Do not assume the total minimum order can be allocated in any way without discussing the specific style.
Describe the inner and outer surface separately when they differ. Include colour, texture, engraving position and artwork. If the finish has a controlling physical reference, identify it.
Review the sample as a physical object
Compare the silhouette and dimensions against the agreed drawing. Review the inner surface, edges, finish and logo legibility. Record observations against the sample revision and make required changes explicit. Do not approve a size or fit solely from a product photograph.
Samples usually take 30 calendar days. Production takes 30–35 calendar days. Those periods do not include an assumed delivery promise to your warehouse.
Start the ring brief
Send the style reference, views or CAD, material, finish, size breakdown and branding requirements. Petra's collection can provide a starting direction; individual material and customization options are reviewed for the selected style. For original development, send your design brief.

pages.title: Stainless Steel Necklace and Pendant Manufacturing | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Plan stainless steel necklace and pendant manufacturing with a complete brief covering the pendant, chain, connections, closure and finished length.

headings.text: Stainless Steel Necklace and Pendant Manufacturing
Keep component and finish choices aligned
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
Petra develops jewelry from an existing collection reference or from a brand's original brief. Stainless steel is our main focus, with silver and brass options available when the design calls for them.
Map the complete assembly
Give the pendant its own dimensions and views. Then show how it connects to the chain, including the orientation you want when worn. Specify the chain direction, intended length, extension arrangement if any, and fastening preference. Identify which elements are fixed and which you want the manufacturer to review.
If the pendant includes engraving, show the artwork and its location. If it includes stones or other components, identify the intended layout and ask for the options relevant to the design. Avoid describing an unconfirmed reference image as a finalized specification.
Keep component and finish choices aligned
A necklace may contain several visible components. Record the intended appearance for the chain, pendant, connector, clasp and any branded tag. If contrast is intentional, mark it. If the finish should be visually consistent, make that requirement explicit in the sample review.
Check the complete assembly physically. The way a pendant sits, the movement of the connection and access to the closure are difficult to judge from a single flat image.
Use this brief checklist
| Include | What it clarifies | 
|---|---|
| Pendant views and dimensions | Shape, proportion and detail | 
| Chain reference and length | The intended necklace configuration | 
| Connection and closure | How the parts join and fasten | 
| Finish reference | Colour, texture and component consistency | 
| Branding artwork | Placement and scale of personal details | 
| Quantity by style | The scope to be quoted | 
Our MOQ is 200 units per style in one colour. Samples usually take 30 calendar days and production takes 30–35 calendar days. Include the target date in your enquiry so timing can be reviewed for the actual project.
Explore the collection for starting references, or send an original necklace brief. Identify the individual styles you want reviewed; an image's colour alone does not confirm its underlying material.

pages.title: Build a Jewelry Development Record Your Team Can Reuse | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Copy a jewelry development record to track drawings, samples, revisions and decisions. Keep one clear reference when your project changes hands.

headings.text: Build a Jewelry Development Record Your Team Can Reuse
Give each style a stable identity
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
The worksheet below is a proposed way for a brand to organize its project. It is not a client case study or a claim about a completed Petra production run.
Give each style a stable identity
Use a style ID that stays the same through development. Give drawings, samples and finish references their own revisions. A revised drawing should not silently replace the file used to approve an earlier sample.
Keep a short description beside the ID so someone outside the design team can identify the piece. Record the material and finish as confirmed, proposed or undecided. Those states should be visible without opening every attachment.
Copy this record structure
| Field | What to enter | 
|---|---|
| Style and description | Your stable reference and product name | 
| Current drawing | File name and revision | 
| Material and finish | Selected specification or unresolved question | 
| Sample reference | The exact piece being discussed | 
| Observation | What the review actually found | 
| Decision | Keep, revise or investigate | 
| Required change | A specific instruction with a marked reference | 
| Open question | What still needs an answer | 
| Next review | What will be checked when the revision arrives | 
Leave a field undecided when the answer is not known. A plausible guess can travel through a project as though someone approved it.
Keep a short decision history
For each revision, record what changed and why. Separate a design preference from a problem against an agreed requirement. This helps the team understand whether a later discussion is reopening a choice or correcting an error.
For example, “change the pendant proportions to match drawing B” is clearer than “use the updated design.” This is an illustrative instruction, not a manufacturing result.
Use the record at handover
Before handing the project to another team member, check that they can find the governing drawing, finish reference and sample decision without asking which attachment is current. Archive superseded files with their revision labels instead of mixing them into the active set.
When you brief Petra, send the active reference package and highlight the questions you want reviewed. Our development process starts with the brief, manufacturing review and a proposed route to sampling.

pages.title: Specifying Stainless Steel for Jewelry: Questions Beyond the Grade Name | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Specify stainless steel jewelry beyond the grade name. Record component materials, finish requirements, open questions and supporting documentation.

headings.text: Specifying Stainless Steel for Jewelry: Questions Beyond the Grade Name
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
This guide helps you prepare that discussion. It does not recommend a universal grade, claim that Petra stocks a particular grade, or substitute for product-specific material or compliance advice.
Define what the designation covers
Ask which material is proposed for the main body and which materials apply to other components. A necklace or earring can include several parts; one material label should not be assumed to describe every part unless that has been established.
Record the full designation and the standard or specification used to identify it. If a supplier uses a general description such as “stainless steel,” ask what more precise information is available for the project rather than filling in a familiar grade yourself.
Separate material, finish and evidence
| Question | Why it belongs in the brief | 
|---|---|
| What material is proposed for each relevant component? | Establishes the scope of the material description | 
| What document supports that description? | Identifies evidence rather than relying on a product name | 
| Which item or batch does the document cover? | Helps connect the evidence to the order | 
| What finish is proposed? | Keeps the surface specification separate from the base material | 
| What claims will the brand make? | Reveals which claims need additional support | 
Do not treat a grade name as proof of a claim such as “hypoallergenic,” “nickel-free” or “waterproof.” Define the exact claim and obtain appropriate evidence for the relevant product and market before using it in customer-facing copy.
Bring uncertainty into the discussion
If you are comparing material options, explain the design, intended use, appearance and documentation requirements. Ask the manufacturer to identify the proposed choice and any questions that remain. Avoid turning an early recommendation into a final specification without recording the decision.
Keep the selected material information with the drawing and sample record. For a repeat order, reference that same specification and explicitly flag any proposed substitution.
Prepare a useful enquiry
Send the product type, drawings or references, desired finish, quantity and target market, plus any existing material requirement. If the material is undecided, say so. Petra's focus is stainless steel, with silver and brass also available; send the project for review so the discussion stays specific to your design.

pages.title: A Jewelry Manufacturing Brief You Can Copy | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Copy Petra’s jewelry manufacturing brief to define materials, finish, quantity, branding and open questions before sampling.

headings.text: A Jewelry Manufacturing Brief You Can Copy
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
Manufacturing brief worksheet
A Jewelry Manufacturing Brief You Can Copy
A clear brief makes the first manufacturing conversation more useful. It tells the supplier what you want to make, what is already decided and where you need advice. You do not need finished CAD to begin, but you do need a way to distinguish requirements from references.
Use the worksheet below for an original design or a private-label shortlist. Keep one row per style and attach the drawings or images that explain it.
- Design
- Specification
- Quantity
- Questions
The project summary
Write a short paragraph covering your brand, the collection direction, the product types and the markets you intend to serve. Add your target date and target price if they are established. Mark them as targets so they are not mistaken for an agreed quotation or production commitment.
For a private-label enquiry, identify the existing styles you want reviewed. For an original design, explain which details are your own and which images are only references for mood, proportion or finish.
The style worksheet
| Field | Your entry | 
|---|---|
| Style ID and product type | Name each ring, necklace, bracelet or earring style | 
| Design reference | Attach drawing, CAD, sketch or collection reference | 
| Key dimensions | State the dimensions already decided | 
| Material | Specify the material or request a review of options | 
| Finish | Include colour, texture and a reference where available | 
| Quantity | List units by style and colour | 
| Branding | Show logo, artwork, location and orientation | 
| Packaging | Describe presentation, labeling and packing requirements | 
| Documentation | List any specific reports or evidence you require | 
| Open questions | Identify the decisions you want help resolving | 
Mark priorities clearly
Use “required,” “preferred” and “open for review.” A required shape or dimension should not look the same as an optional idea. This makes it easier to assess alternatives without losing the design's purpose.
For each attachment, include a short note explaining what it demonstrates. “Use this as a surface-texture reference” is more precise than sending an image with no instruction. Keep file names and revision labels consistent across the brief.
Check the brief before sending
Read it as someone seeing the project for the first time. Can they identify the styles, understand which material and finish choices are settled, and find the intended quantities? Can they see which questions need answers? Remove conflicting older files from the active reference set.
Petra's MOQ is 200 units per style in one colour. Samples usually take 30 calendar days; production takes 30–35 calendar days. Include your intended range and timing in the brief so the proposal addresses the actual scope.
The worksheet is public and can be copied without a download form. When ready, send your brief to Petra, or browse existing collection designs to build a private-label shortlist.
Tell us what you want to make.
MOQ: 200 units per style, one colour. Samples usually 30 calendar days. Production 30–35 calendar days.

pages.title: Silver Jewelry Manufacturing for Your Collection | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Bring your silver jewelry designs or collection references to Petra for development, sampling and manufacturing review.

headings.text: Silver Jewelry Manufacturing for Your Collection
Build the material into the brief
Review the design as a complete piece
Use sampling to settle the details
Send the silver project for review
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
Start from an existing Petra style or your own brief. Identify the material specification and finish you want reviewed rather than relying on appearance alone. A silver-coloured photograph does not establish the underlying material.
Build the material into the brief
Send the proposed silver specification with your design, dimensions, construction and finish references. If the specification is undecided, make that an explicit question. Include any marking or documentation requirements relevant to your product and market so they can be considered before the scope is finalized.
Do not assume a mark, a material document or a particular product claim is included merely because the project is described as silver jewelry. Those details belong in the project discussion.
Review the design as a complete piece
For a ring, show the profile, size requirements and artwork. For a necklace, define the pendant, chain and connection. For earrings and bracelets, include fastening, movement and the dimensions that matter to the design.
Where stone setting or contrasting finishes are part of the brief, use marked references to show their position and appearance. Petra's services include CAD development, sampling, stone setting, polishing, engraving and packaging; the proposal should identify the work relevant to your piece.
Use sampling to settle the details
Compare the physical sample against the agreed drawing and finish reference. Record decisions about shape, dimensions, surface appearance, construction and branding. Keep unresolved material or documentation questions visible rather than treating an attractive sample as proof of every requirement.
Our MOQ is 200 units per style in one colour. Samples usually take 30 calendar days, and production takes 30–35 calendar days. Share the intended quantities and target date in your first message.
Send the silver project for review
Prepare the design or style reference, proposed material, finish direction, quantity, artwork and packaging requirements. If you are comparing silver with stainless steel, explain the priorities behind the choice rather than asking for a universal “better” material.
Discuss your silver jewelry project or explore the existing collection. Material and customization options are reviewed for the individual styles you select.

pages.title: Stainless Steel or Silver? Build the Decision Around the Collection | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Compare stainless steel and silver around your jewelry collection’s design, material specification, finish, documentation and sample requirements.

headings.text: Stainless Steel or Silver? Build the Decision Around the Collection
Check the language your brand will use
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
Petra's main focus is stainless steel, with silver available as a second material direction. If both are under consideration, prepare one clear design brief and ask for the differences to be assessed against that same brief.
Keep the comparison fair
Two proposals are difficult to compare if they cover different dimensions, construction, finishes or packaging. Identify what stays constant and what changes with the material option. Ask for assumptions to be stated rather than comparing headline prices alone.
| Compare | What to establish for each option | 
|---|---|
| Material specification | The exact proposed material and relevant components | 
| Design | Shape, dimensions, construction and any proposed changes | 
| Finish | Colour, texture and the reference used for approval | 
| Branding and presentation | Artwork, markings and packaging included | 
| Commercial scope | Quantity, quoted work and exclusions | 
| Evidence | Documentation needed for the claims you intend to make | 
This comparison table is a buying tool. It does not assign unverified cost, durability or performance scores to either material.
Review the physical samples
Compare the complete pieces against your intended design. Record their measured dimensions and your observations about appearance and handling. If weight is part of the decision, measure the actual samples rather than borrowing a generic number from a different design.
Keep preference separate from specification. Your team may prefer the appearance of one sample while still needing changes to its proportions or finish. Record both observations so the material decision does not hide outstanding development work.
Check the language your brand will use
Material names, performance claims and care instructions should reflect the actual product and supporting evidence. Avoid treating colour, a grade name or an informal description as proof of a safety or durability promise.
For the US, UK or European market, identify the product-specific documentation and labeling questions relevant to the collection. Resolve those with qualified support where needed; a comparison article cannot establish a product's compliance.
Make a recorded decision
Document the selected option, the reasons for choosing it and any open requirements. Retain the other proposal as a comparison record rather than leaving two conflicting specifications in the active brief.
Send Petra the design and material options you want reviewed. A clear comparison brief is the starting point for a useful manufacturing proposal.

pages.title: Stainless Steel Earring Manufacturing: Brief the Pair, Not Just the Shape | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Brief a stainless steel earring project with pair orientation, dimensions, fastening and finish requirements. Start a manufacturing discussion with Petra.

headings.text: Stainless Steel Earring Manufacturing: Brief the Pair, Not Just the Shape
Review more than the front view
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
Petra reviews original designs and existing collection references for brands. Stainless steel is the main focus, with silver and brass options available when the project requires them.
Show how the pair works
Identify whether the earrings are identical, mirrored or intentionally different. Use front and side views to explain the shape, and show the position of any post, hook, hinge or other proposed fastening. For moving or suspended elements, illustrate the intended relationship between parts.
State the dimensions and any weight target already established by your team. Treat an untested target as a requirement to review, not as an achieved product specification.
Define the relevant components
Ask which material is proposed for the main body and for the components that form the fastening. Keep those details in the record rather than assuming one material description covers everything. If your brand needs specific documentation or wants to make a particular product claim, bring that requirement into the brief.
Specify the colour and surface appearance across the pair. Show engraving, stone positions or contrasting areas with marked artwork or drawings. A collection photograph can be a useful style reference without proving the material or construction of the proposed item.
Review more than the front view
When the sample is ready, examine the pair together and individually. Compare the shape, orientation, dimensions, surface and branding against the reference. Review the fastening and movement physically. Record observations clearly and avoid turning a short sample review into an unsupported wear or safety claim.
If a detail changes, identify whether it affects one side or both. Keep the revised drawing and sample reference together so a mirrored design does not become a source of conflicting instructions.
Start with a complete enquiry
Send your references, views, dimensions, intended materials, finish and quantity. Petra's MOQ is 200 units per style in one colour; state how you count the earring product and packing units so the quote uses the same basis. Samples usually take 30 calendar days and production takes 30–35 calendar days.
Send your earring brief or browse the collection for starting directions. The specific style's material and customization options are confirmed during project review.

pages.title: A Finish Review Worksheet for Jewelry Collections | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Copy a jewelry finish review worksheet to record references, viewing conditions, observations and actions before choosing the collection’s finish.

headings.text: A Finish Review Worksheet for Jewelry Collections
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
This is a visual review worksheet, not a laboratory test report. It does not establish a coating's thickness, lifespan or resistance to a particular exposure.
Prepare the comparison
Identify the sample, material, finish reference and revision. Review the sample and reference under the same conditions, and record those conditions if another person will repeat the comparison. Keep photographs as supporting evidence; do not assume a photograph captures every visible difference.
For a collection, select representative forms such as a flat face, a curved surface and a small component where applicable. The point is to make the review explicit rather than declaring the whole collection approved from one image.
Copy the worksheet
| Field | Record | 
|---|---|
| Style and sample revision | The exact piece under review | 
| Finish reference | Physical reference or agreed specification ID | 
| Review conditions | Lighting and comparison setup | 
| Area inspected | Face, edge, recess, inner surface or component | 
| Observation | The visible difference, if any | 
| Required action | Accept, revise or request clarification | 
| Supporting image | File name linked to the observation | 
| Open evidence | Any test or document still required | 
Keep appearance feedback separate from performance evidence. If the brand requires a particular test, define that requirement and ask how it will be met. Do not label this sheet a “pass certificate.”
Make the feedback precise
Describe the location and reference. “Review the texture on the outer face against reference B” is actionable. “Make it more premium” leaves the desired change undefined. If two reviewers prefer different outcomes, settle the intended direction before requesting a revision.
Use a new revision record when the finish changes. Keep the previous decision so your team can trace why a sample was accepted or returned for review.
Retain the chosen reference
When the finish is agreed, keep its identifier with the drawing, sample and order brief. Use that reference when discussing a repeat order or an extension to the collection. A new style still needs its own review where the shape or construction changes the appearance.
Petra reviews finishing options around the material and design. Send your finish reference and project details, or explore the services overview before preparing the brief.

pages.title: Preparing a Silver Jewelry Sample Review | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Prepare a silver jewelry sample review using the material record, drawing, finish reference and artwork. Record decisions and unresolved questions.

headings.text: Preparing a Silver Jewelry Sample Review
Plan the next stage from the actual decision
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
Gather the current drawing, sample reference, finish reference and artwork before the review. Confirm which revision each file represents.
Check the material record
Record the proposed silver specification and any relevant component materials. Identify the documentation or marking requirements already discussed for the project. If a requirement is unresolved, keep it open rather than inferring the answer from the piece's colour or a photograph.
For any marking included in the design, check its agreed artwork, location and legibility. Whether a particular mark is appropriate for the product and destination market is a separate question that needs the relevant evidence and advice.
Review the physical design
Compare the shape, dimensions, proportions and construction against the drawing. Examine the surface, edges, joins and any setting or fastening details relevant to the style. Handle the piece so the review includes movement and access to closures where applicable.
If the sample includes a surface finish, compare it against the intended reference and identify the specific areas under review. Do not collapse the base material and surface appearance into a single “silver finish” description if they represent different decisions.
Record the outcome
| Record | Purpose | 
|---|---|
| Style, drawing and sample revisions | Identifies what was reviewed | 
| Material and finish references | Separates the governing specifications | 
| Measured dimensions | Makes size observations explicit | 
| Visual and functional observations | Describes what the review found | 
| Required changes | Gives one clear revision list | 
| Open documentation questions | Prevents an unresolved item becoming an assumed approval | 
Separate required corrections from optional design changes. When the team agrees a revision, update the active record and retain the earlier version for reference.
Plan the next stage from the actual decision
An approved appearance is not automatically approval of unresolved packaging, documentation or other requirements. Make the sample decision specific enough that the next person handling the project understands its scope.
Petra's samples usually take 30 calendar days; production takes 30–35 calendar days. The minimum order is 200 units per style in one colour. Send your silver jewelry brief with the specifications and review requirements you want considered.

pages.title: How to Brief a Repeat Stainless Steel Jewelry Order | Petra Jewelry
pages.description: Brief a repeat stainless steel jewelry order with approved references, unchanged requirements, intended changes and the proposed quantity allocation.

headings.text: How to Brief a Repeat Stainless Steel Jewelry Order
Bring previous observations into the brief
Confirm the scope of the new order
Tell us what you want to make.

pages.text:
Use the previous style and sample references, then build a short list of unchanged requirements, intended changes and questions still open.
Re-establish the reference
Identify the style, drawing revision, material specification, finish reference and approved sample. Include the packaging and artwork versions that should be used. If your team has more than one reference sample, make clear which one governs the order.
Keep the product description consistent with the earlier record. A new marketing name should not obscure the manufacturing style identifier.
Separate changes from repeats
| Item | Confirm or update | 
|---|---|
| Design and dimensions | The governing drawing and any intended revision | 
| Material and finish | Existing specification or proposed change | 
| Quantity | Units by style, colour and agreed allocation | 
| Branding | Artwork version and placement | 
| Packaging | Presentation, labels and packing requirements | 
| Documentation | Reports or evidence required for this order | 
| Timing | Target date to be reviewed in the proposal | 
If a finish, component or design feature is changing, ask whether another sample review is needed. A deliberate revision should not be hidden inside a repeat-order label.
Bring previous observations into the brief
Record any concrete issue your team wants reviewed. Identify the product and observation, attach the relevant evidence, and state the requested action. Keep customer preference, inspection findings and proposed design improvements distinct so the manufacturer understands the purpose of each note.
Do not promise a result before the issue has been assessed. “Review this closure detail” is a request; “this change will eliminate returns” is an outcome that needs evidence.
Confirm the scope of the new order
Ask for a proposal reflecting the current quantity and requirements. Do not assume a previous quote, lead time or material option automatically applies to a new scope.
Petra's MOQ is 200 units per style in one colour. Production takes 30–35 calendar days, with samples usually taking 30 calendar days when sampling is needed. Discuss the timing for the actual repeat project rather than combining those figures into an assumed arrival date.
Send your repeat-order references and highlight changes at the top of the message. A clean reference package makes the manufacturing discussion easier to follow.
